stem.text: Let \( y = f(x) \) be the particular solution to the differential equation \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = xy \) with the initial condition \( f(1) = 2 \).

parts.prompt: Find \( \dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \) in terms of \( x \) and \( y \), and evaluate it at the point \( (1, 2) \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate xy with the product rule and substitute dy/dx.

points.criterion: Gives y(1 + x^2), or an equivalent expression in x and y, and the value 4 at (1, 2).

parts.prompt: The line tangent to the graph of \( f \) at \( x = 1 \) is used to approximate \( f(1.3) \), giving the value 2.6. Is this approximation an overestimate or an underestimate of \( f(1.3) \)? Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: y starts at 2 and dy/dx = xy is positive while y is, so y stays positive for 1 <= x <= 1.3.
So the second derivative is positive on the whole interval; the graph is concave up and lies above its tangent line.

points.criterion: Concludes underestimate because the second derivative is positive (f is concave up) on the interval from x = 1 to x = 1.3, not only at x = 1, so the tangent line lies below the graph.
